Assessment, incorporating FSR insights:
- Policy stance: Strongly accommodative at the zero lower bound with a symmetric 2% inflation objective. Continued Treasury and agency MBS/CMBS purchases, plus active repo and ON RRP operations, reinforce forward guidance and QE, easing term premia and supporting mortgage credit transmission.
- FSR context on risks: COVID-19 continues to weigh on activity and inflation; risk appetite fell and uncertainty remains high. Vulnerabilities are elevated in SMEs and households, with rising delinquencies; nonbank mortgage servicers face funding/operational strains that could impair lending; CRE valuation pressures persist; sectoral stress (energy, airlines, leisure) raises default risks. March 2020 funding dislocations in Treasury and dollar funding markets have eased with policy support but remain sensitive to shocks.
- Backstops and market functioning: The FSR highlights that facilities and asset purchases (CPFF, SMCCF, MLF, TALF, FIMA repo, expanded swap lines) helped restore market functioning and credit availability, tempering downside risks.

Net tone: Cautiously negative given elevated vulnerabilities and virus-driven uncertainty, but moderated by credible policy backstops and improved market functioning.
